dedupe_keys.name: general transit feed specification gtfs schedule and gtfs realtime

description: The General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) is the community-driven open data standard in which public transport agencies publish their networks and timetables. GTFS Schedule is a zip of CSV text files (agencies, stops, routes, trips, stop times, calendars, shapes, fares, transfers, pathways and flexible services); GTFS Realtime, added in 2011, is a protocol-buffer feed of trip updates, vehicle positions and service alerts. It began as a collaboration between TriMet in Portland and Google, was renamed from the Google to the General Transit Feed Specification in 2010, and since 2019 is maintained by the non-profit MobilityData with the community; gtfs.org states that more than 10,000 agencies in over 100 countries use it. The standard itself has no spatial coverage; feeds built on it describe single networks down to individual stops and departures. The reference, best practices and change history are published on gtfs.org and in the GitHub repository google/transit, whose content is licensed Apache-2.0 and free to use. Caveats: the specification describes rider-facing service, not infrastructure condition or capacity, and optional extensions (fares v2, flex) are unevenly adopted. GTFS is the input format of most transit simulation and accessibility tools (OpenTripPlanner, R5, MATSim via pt2matsim) and underlies network flow, agent-based and capacity planning studies; feeds are found through the Mobility Database and Transitland, both catalogued here.
